docs.title: MobsManager Documentation
docs.text: Per-world mob spawn control for Bukkit ecosystems: Spigot, Paper, Purpur, and other compatible servers. This documentation covers installation, configuration, command usage, and operational behavior.

docs.title: What MobsManager Does
docs.text:
MobsManager lets you decide which mobs may spawn, where they may spawn, and under which spawn categories they remain allowed.

It is built for administrators who want reliable world-by-world control without maintaining a heavy or obscure configuration system.

docs.title: Highlights
docs.text:
• Per-world mob spawn management
  • Fine-grained control by spawn category
  • Compatibility with legacy entity names from older plugin versions
  • Java 17 and Spigot API 1.21.1 support
  • Versioned documentation powered by Material for MkDocs and mike

docs.title: MobsManager - Commands and Permissions
docs.text:
Make sure you have already installed the plugin before using this command reference.

This page documents the current /mm command set and the related permission nodes.

docs.title: Commands
docs.text: Command Permission Description /mm reload mobsmanager.reload Reloads configuration and rebuilds in-memory entity data. /mm enable <Mob> <SpawnReason> <World> mobsmanager.manageEntity Enables one spawn category for an entity. /mm disable <Mob> <SpawnReason> <World> mobsmanager.manageEntity Disables one spawn category for an entity. /mm info <Mob> <World> mobsmanager.info Displays the current spawn configuration for one entity. /mm status <Mob> <World> mobsmanager.info Alias of /mm info. /mm list <World> [Mode] [Page] mobsmanager.info Lists entities for a world. Modes: changed, blocked, all. /mm help mobsmanager.help Displays the built-in command help.

docs.title: Permission Nodes
docs.text: Permission Description mobsmanager.manageEntity Allows enabling or disabling spawn categories. mobsmanager.reload Allows reloading the plugin. mobsmanager.help Allows viewing command help. mobsmanager.info Allows reading mob spawn information.

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• Entity names use Bukkit EntityType names.
  • Legacy entity names are still recognized by the compatibility layer.
  • Use * as the world argument when a command supports targeting all worlds.
  • /mm list <World> shows changed entities by default.
  • /mm list <World> blocked shows only restricted entities.
  • /mm list <World> all shows every managed entity for the world.

docs.title: MobsManager - Configuration
docs.text:
Make sure you have already installed the plugin before editing its configuration.

MobsManager uses two configuration files:

  • config.yml for global plugin settings
  • mobsData.yml for per-world entity spawn rules

After changing config.yml, run /mm reload or restart the server.

docs.title: Global Options
docs.text: Key Type Default Description auto-update boolean true Enables the built-in updater at startup. world-guard-detection boolean false Avoids spawn conflicts when WorldGuard already controls spawn behavior.

docs.title: Data File
docs.text:
mobsData.yml stores the effective spawn rules for each entity in each world.

The plugin maintains this file automatically. In most cases, administrators should prefer plugin commands over manual edits.

docs.title: Compatibility Notes
docs.text: Older saved entity names are normalized automatically when the plugin loads. This helps legacy configurations continue to work on newer Spigot APIs without manual cleanup.

docs.title: Operational Recommendation
docs.text: If you are making several changes in a row, prefer editing your global settings first, then use commands to fine-tune world or entity behavior.

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
The current development branch targets:

  • Java 17
  • Spigot API 1.21.1
  • Bukkit, Spigot, Paper, and compatible Bukkit-based forks

docs.title: Before You Install
docs.text:
Make sure the version you downloaded matches your server and Java runtime.

If you are upgrading from an older release, MobsManager will normalize legacy entity names when it loads. This helps older data files remain usable on newer APIs.

docs.title: MobsManager - How It Works
docs.text: This page explains the core behavior of the plugin.

docs.title: Default Behavior
docs.text:
MobsManager blocks the spawn of entities that you have disabled through its data file and commands. Rules are applied per world, so each world can keep its own spawn policy.

Note

Existing entities are not removed automatically just because future spawning has been disabled.

docs.title: Spawn Categories
docs.text:
MobsManager groups Minecraft spawn reasons into a small set of categories:

  • ALL: blocks every kind of spawn
  • NATURAL: blocks natural or world-driven spawning
  • CUSTOM: blocks command, plugin, transformation, or other non-natural spawning
  • SPAWNER: blocks spawner-driven spawning, including modern spawner variants
  • EGG: blocks spawn egg and related egg-based spawning
  • BREEDING: blocks animal breeding results
  • IRON_GOLEM: blocks spawns triggered by building an iron golem

docs.title: Newer Minecraft Spawn Reasons
docs.text:
Minecraft and Spigot keep introducing new spawn reasons. MobsManager maps newer reasons to the existing categories so that older configurations remain usable without being rewritten from scratch.

Examples:

  • TRIAL_SPAWNER is treated as SPAWNER
  • DISPENSE_EGG is treated as EGG
  • COMMAND is treated as CUSTOM
  • REINFORCEMENTS is treated as NATURAL

docs.title: World-by-World Management
docs.text: Each entity is tracked per world. This means you can allow a mob in one world while blocking the same mob in another.

docs.title: MobsManager - Installation
docs.text: Make sure you have already downloaded the plugin before following these steps.

docs.title: Installation Steps
docs.text:
1. Download the MobsManager-X.X.X.jar file.
  2. Place it in your server's plugins directory.
  3. Start or restart the server.

If everything loads correctly, the console should show a message similar to:

[MobsManager] Enabling MobsManager vX.X.X

docs.title: After Startup
docs.text:
On first start, the plugin generates its configuration files and initializes per-world entity data.

If you are updating from an older version, MobsManager may migrate older entity names automatically so your stored configuration stays compatible with newer APIs.

docs.title: If Startup Fails
docs.text:
• verify that your server software is compatible
  • verify that the server is running Java 17+
  • check the startup log for dependency or API errors
  • ask for help on Discord if needed

docs.title: MobsManager - Troubleshooting
docs.text: This page covers the most common issues you may encounter while installing or operating MobsManager.

docs.title: The Plugin Does Not Load
docs.text:
• verify that your server is running a compatible Bukkit-based implementation
  • verify that your server uses Java 17+
  • check the startup logs for missing dependencies or API incompatibilities

docs.title: My Existing Configuration Changed After Update
docs.text:
This is usually expected when upgrading from older versions.

MobsManager now normalizes legacy entity names to current API names. After startup or after /mm reload, review mobsData.yml if you want to confirm how old names were migrated.

docs.title: Spawns Are Still Not Behaving As Expected
docs.text:
• verify that you changed the correct world
  • verify that you changed the correct spawn category
  • verify that another plugin is not also controlling mob spawns
  • if WorldGuard is installed, review the world-guard-detection setting

docs.title: The Updater Does Not Behave As Expected
docs.text:
MobsManager compares versions by numeric segments.

If you are testing an unreleased development version or a new major version, auto-update may intentionally refuse to download the remote build.

docs.title: Still Stuck?
docs.text: If the issue persists, open an issue on GitHub or ask for help on Discord.
